catalog_quote: Stress in Galician may fall on any of the last three syllables of a word. If a word has a closed syllable in final position, stress usually falls on that syllable, e.g. final [fiˈnal] 'end', roncón [roŋˈkoŋ] 'pipe in a bagpipe', armar [arˈmar] 'to arm'. In certain loans and learned words stress may be on the penultimate syllable, as in revólver [reˈβolβer] 'revolver', dolmen [ˈdɔlmɛŋ] 'dolmen', útil [ˈutil] 'useful'. If there is a final open syllable in a word, stress will normally fall on the penultimate syllable, e.g. casa [ˈkɑsa] 'house', home [ˈɔme] 'man', carballo [kɑrˈβaʎo] 'oak', edificio [eðiˈfiθjo] 'building'. However, some words end in a stressed vowel, e.g. avó [aˈβo] 'grandfather', alá [aˈla] 'over there'. sources.quote: p.197-198: apart from passing remarks in grammars (Álvarez/Regueira/Monteagudo 1986:305; Álvarez/Xove 2002:245) only Parafita Couto 2007 treats Galician verb stress. p.204-205: the most common pattern in the regular conjugation is 'acento en la penúltima sílaba', proposed as default V[σ' σ]w, with listed exceptions (infinitive cantar, 1sg cantei, 1/2pl cantásemos/cantásedes antepenult, futures). p.225: 'la posición del acento en el verbo gallego no es sensible a la cantidad' (2pl.imp cantade, cantai, cantá all stress the theme vowel regardless of suffix shape); stress position is anchored to m
sources.locator: pp. 197-198 (state of research), pp. 204-205 (default pattern (6)), pp. 225-226 (Conclusiones)
sources.note: Only open stress-specific study of Galician found; shows verb stress is quantity-insensitive and morphologically anchored (default penult), supporting lexical over a weight-driven reading; downloaded now.
